text:
Macklin Celebrini is 20, wears the C in San Jose, and plays almost 23 minutes a night like it's the most normal thing in the world. Thirty-three points in 26 games, 13 of them on the power play. Among forwards picked in the top three since 2005, the median first full season is 0.55 points a game. He's at 1.27.

The interesting part is that he's probably been a little unlucky. He's shooting 10.7%, below the 13.8% our numbers think is his true level, and his on-ice results trail the chances his lines create. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards last season for setting up shots, which is the profile of a player whose assists keep coming whether or not his own shots fall.

Friday he scored the empty-netter that sealed the first regulation win in Sharks history over Vegas at SAP Center. That's the kind of small milestone a rebuild remembers. Our range has him finishing between 94 and 122 points. Watch his finishing: when it turns, the numbers jump.
